stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under key NLP/ML tags such as 'transformers', 'llama', and 'text-generation'.
This indicates continued community interest and practical application of Meta's latest open-source LLMs.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It pertains to the core field of large language models (LLMs) and text generation.
The associated tags indicate relevance to transformers, safetensors, and the Llama family of models.

stories.title: The first self-driving vehicle on Mars has proven to be a smashing success
stories.author: Eric Berger
bullet_points: Perseverance rover on Mars has demonstrated significant autonomous driving capabilities.
Approximately 90% of the distance covered by the rover has been driven without human intervention.
This marks a major milestone in autonomous systems operating in extreme extraterrestrial environments.

stories.title: DeepMind’s hurricane breakthrough has surprised weather scientists
stories.author: Victoria Turk, wired.com
bullet_points: DeepMind has achieved a significant breakthrough in weather prediction using AI.
The open-source WeatherNext model demonstrates accuracy even with lower-resolution weather data.
The findings have surprised established weather scientists, indicating a potential shift in forecasting capabilities.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance saw up to 90% speedup when tested on the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher quality outputs, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, offering an open-source framework for building personal AI agents.
The key feature is that these agents can run entirely on the user's local hardware, enhancing privacy and control.
It features built-in support for Ollama, leveraging local LLM execution capabilities.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for performance gains.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware, optimizing local AI inference.
The feature is currently available in a preview state, indicating active development and adoption.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with messaging applications.
It utilizes local AI coding agents, emphasizing on-device processing for privacy and control.
The core value proposition is connecting communication platforms to local, private AI capabilities.

stories.title: Judge rules Meta caused "public nuisance" and must fund mental health treatment
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: A New Mexico judge ruled that Meta caused a 'public nuisance' related to its platforms.
The ruling mandates that Meta fund a $567 million initiative to address the youth mental health crisis.
This case represents a significant legal action holding a major tech company accountable for societal impact.

stories.title: On-Policy Self-Distillation without Any Supervision
stories.author: Nuno Vasconcelos
bullet_points: Introduces a method for On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPD) that eliminates the need for external supervision.
The technique leverages only the model's own generations and internal consistency for training.
Addresses a key limitation in existing LLM fine-tuning methods that rely heavily on ground-truth or external guidance.

stories.title: Beyond Top-K: Replacing Black-Box Retrieval with Interpretable Agentic Operations
stories.author: Tabarakul Hazarika
bullet_points: Challenges the standard 'chunk-embed-top-k' paradigm in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG).
Argues the standard approach is structurally unsound for complex, structured documents like financial reports.
Proposes replacing black-box retrieval with more interpretable, agentic operations for better accuracy.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings improved performance and expanded GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to enhance model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically improving capabilities on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for advanced AI features within Claude Code.
The new capabilities include the implementation of 'subagents' for more complex task decomposition.
Web search functionality has been added to enhance the knowledge base and real-time capability of Claude Code.

stories.title: X replaces its revenue-sharing program with ‘Original Content Rewards’
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: X is discontinuing its previous revenue-sharing program for content creators.
A new initiative, 'Original Content Rewards,' will launch on September 8th.
Eligibility for the new program requires creators to have 500+ verified followers and 500,000+ Home Timeline impressions.

stories.title: An Amazon data center could have the worst polluting power plant in the country
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: Amazon is investing in a new power plant in West Texas to support a new data center.
The proposed gas-burning power plant could become one of the largest single sources of greenhouse gases in the US.
The story highlights the environmental impact associated with large-scale tech infrastructure buildouts.

stories.title: Europe's free satellite service just made it easier to track wildfires
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Copernicus Browser, a free European satellite service, has been updated to include wildfire visualization.
The update aims to improve tracking capabilities during a period of record wildfire seasons.
This represents a practical application of satellite data for environmental monitoring and disaster response.

stories.title: Learning When to Trust via Selective Context Preference Optimization
stories.author: Lingdong Kong
bullet_points: Addresses the vulnerability of language models to misleading external context signals.
Proposes 'selective trust' as a solution, moving beyond simple context resistance.
Introduces MIST, a new human-annotated benchmark to test conditional trust in reasoning.

stories.title: Tracing the Heart: An Evidence-Linked Pipeline for Heart-Failure Feature Engineering
stories.author: Priyadarshini Kachroo
bullet_points: The paper addresses the significant bottleneck of EHR feature engineering in clinical AI, which consumes 39-45% of data scientists' time.
It focuses specifically on heart failure, a prevalent condition requiring complex integration of fragmented EHR data with clinical guidelines.
The proposed pipeline aims to improve upon existing rule-based and LLM approaches by providing evidence-linked, more maintainable automation.

stories.title: AV-AIVAT: 74x Cheaper Agent Evaluation with Certified Anytime-Valid Stopping in Imperfect-Information Games
stories.author: Longbo Huang
bullet_points: Introduces AV-AIVAT, a new method for evaluating AI agents in imperfect-information games.
Addresses the inefficiency of traditional agent evaluation by allowing for 'Anytime-Valid Stopping'.
Claims to achieve up to 74x cost reduction in evaluation while maintaining statistical guarantees.

stories.title: The Low Frequency Trap: Video Language Models Fail at Simple Event Bookkeeping
stories.author: Furong Huang
bullet_points: Video Language Models (VLMs) struggle with granular event bookkeeping in real-world video data.
Existing benchmarks either lack control (real-world clips) or lack auditing capability (programmatic benchmarks).
The paper introduces 'trace-grounded parametric profiling' to accurately count events in controlled video tasks.

stories.title: Challenges in Evaluating Explanation Methods for Static and Evolving Data
stories.author: Jerzy Stefanowski
bullet_points: The paper addresses critical limitations in current Explainable AI (XAI) evaluation methods.
It demonstrates issues using the DetoxAI system for bias detection and concept unlearning in image recognition.
Research explores adapting explanation techniques, such as counterfactuals, to handle evolving data streams and concept drift.

stories.title: TRAJDEBUG: Tracing Error Lifecycle to Identify Critical Failures in Long-Horizon Agent Trajectories
stories.author: Juanzi Li
bullet_points: Introduces TRAJDEBUG, a method designed to trace the error lifecycle in long-horizon agent trajectories.
Addresses a key challenge in LLM-based agentic systems: identifying the earliest root cause of cascading failures.
Focuses on the difficulty of error detection when evidence is scattered across long sequences of instructions and observations.

stories.title: Tytan: Interactive Neurosymbolic Construction of Analytic Semantic Schemas from Relational Data
stories.author: Kristian J. Hammond
bullet_points: Introduces TYTAN, a system designed to automatically construct analytic semantic schemas from relational data.
Addresses the 'knowledge-acquisition bottleneck' where data understanding (entities, measures, relationships) is currently done manually.
Aims to improve data analysis scalability and reduce dependency on domain experts for non-technical users.

stories.title: Learning When to Trust via Selective Context Preference Optimization
stories.author: Lingdong Kong
bullet_points: Addresses the vulnerability of language models to misleading external context signals.
Introduces 'selective trust' as a new paradigm, moving beyond simple context resistance.
Presents MIST, a new human-annotated benchmark designed to test context reliance under various conditions.

stories.title: Tracing the Heart: An Evidence-Linked Pipeline for Heart-Failure Feature Engineering
stories.author: Priyadarshini Kachroo
bullet_points: The paper addresses the significant bottleneck of EHR feature engineering in clinical AI, which consumes a large portion of data scientists' time.
It focuses specifically on heart failure, a condition requiring complex integration of fragmented EHR data with clinical guidelines.
The proposed pipeline aims to improve upon existing rule-based and LLM approaches by providing evidence-linked and more maintainable feature engineering.

stories.title: AV-AIVAT: 74x Cheaper Agent Evaluation with Certified Anytime-Valid Stopping in Imperfect-Information Games
stories.author: Longbo Huang
bullet_points: Introduces AV-AIVAT, a new method for evaluating AI agents in imperfect-information games.
Addresses the high cost and uncertainty of traditional agent comparison methods (e.g., game playing).
Provides a certified anytime-valid stopping criterion, ensuring evaluation accuracy without fixed budget waste.

stories.title: CalibForge: Adversarial Solver Calibration for Scaling Learnable Terminal Tasks
stories.author: Kai Jia
bullet_points: Introduces CalibForge, a system for autonomous terminal-task synthesis in reinforcement learning.
The system uses adversarial solver calibration to ensure generated tasks are appropriately challenging for learning agents.
Addresses the gap where simple task executability does not guarantee optimal difficulty relative to the solver's capabilities.

stories.title: RRC: Unlocking Generative Reward Models in LLM Reinforcement Learning via Ranking-Based Reward Construction
stories.author: Jingbo Zhu
bullet_points: The paper addresses a limitation in applying generative reward models (GRMs) to Reinforcement Learning (RL).
The core issue identified is the mismatch between GRMs' comparative nature and RL's scalar scoring requirement.
The authors propose a novel method (RRC) to bridge this gap and unlock the potential of GRMs in LLM RL.

stories.title: HarnessOpt-Bench: Evaluating LLMs at Harness Optimization
stories.author: Yuan Xue
bullet_points: The performance of Large Language Models (LLMs) is increasingly dependent on the 'harness' (prompts, tools, control flow, etc.) surrounding them, not just the model weights.
Automated harness optimization—using AI to iteratively improve the surrounding system—is identified as a crucial, yet challenging, area for AI advancement.
The research highlights a current lack of a standardized protocol within the community for measuring and evaluating these complex LLM harnesses.

stories.title: Learning When to Trust via Selective Context Preference Optimization
stories.author: Lingdong Kong
bullet_points: Addresses the vulnerability of language models to misleading external context signals.
Proposes 'selective trust' as a solution, moving beyond simply training models to ignore all context.
Introduces MIST, a new human-annotated benchmark designed to test context reliability under various conditions.

stories.title: The Bitter Lesson of Tool Calling
stories.author: Vamse Kumar Subbiah
bullet_points: The paper investigates how programmatic tool calling (PTC) evolves LLMs into more capable agents compared to native JSON tool calling.
PTC allows code-capable models to chain and parallelize actions naturally, moving beyond rigid data structures.
The research addresses a gap by empirically comparing PTC against native JSON tool calling on established benchmarks under real-world conditions.

stories.title: AV-AIVAT: 74x Cheaper Agent Evaluation with Certified Anytime-Valid Stopping in Imperfect-Information Games
stories.author: Longbo Huang
bullet_points: Introduces AV-AIVAT, a method for evaluating AI agents in imperfect-information games.
Addresses the inefficiency of traditional evaluation methods by allowing for certified anytime-valid stopping.
Offers a solution to the problem of unknown game counts, ensuring evaluation stops as soon as sufficient evidence is gathered while maintaining statistical guarantees.

stories.title: RP-OPSD: Reasoning-Pivot-Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation for Multilingual Reasoning Transfer
stories.author: Shujian Huang
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenge of multilingual reasoning transfer in Large Language Models (LLMs).
It proposes RP-OPSD, a novel method that enhances On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) by incorporating reasoning-pivot guidance.
The core contribution is explicitly prioritizing reasoning signals during distillation to improve cross-lingual transfer capabilities.

stories.title: Benchmarking the Benchmarks: Evaluating Benchmarks for Conversational Agents
stories.author: Abigail Goldsteen
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical issue of poor quality in existing benchmarks used to evaluate task-oriented conversational agents.
It introduces a novel, reference-free framework that leverages LLM judges to assess benchmark quality.
This framework provides actionable diagnostics regarding a benchmark's consistency, complexity, and policy coverage.

stories.title: Benchmarking and Enhancing LLMs for Rule-Intensive Review of National Standard Documents
stories.author: Tianyong Hao
bullet_points: The paper addresses a gap in LLM evaluation: their performance on rule-intensive document review.
National standard documents (e.g., China GB/T) are proposed as a challenging, structured testbed for LLMs.
Current LLM benchmarks are criticized for focusing too much on domain knowledge rather than intrinsic rule adherence.

stories.title: RRC: Unlocking Generative Reward Models in LLM Reinforcement Learning via Ranking-Based Reward Construction
stories.author: Jingbo Zhu
bullet_points: Addresses a gap in LLM Reinforcement Learning (RL) by focusing on generative reward models.
Identifies a core limitation: the mismatch between generative models' comparative nature and RL's scalar scoring requirement.
Proposes a novel method (RRC) to bridge this gap and unlock the potential of generative reward models in RL.

stories.title: HarnessOpt-Bench: Evaluating LLMs at Harness Optimization
stories.author: Yuan Xue
bullet_points: The paper introduces HarnessOpt-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating Large Language Models (LLMs) within agentic systems.
It highlights that LLM performance heavily relies on the 'harness' (prompts, tools, control flow, etc.), not just the model weights.
The work addresses the need for automated harness optimization—AI-driven improvement of the surrounding system—which is currently lacking a common evaluation protocol.

stories.title: Shopify replaced Redis with MySQL for inventory reservations–and it scaled
stories.author: adletbalzhanov
bullet_points: Shopify made a significant architectural change by replacing Redis with MySQL for inventory reservations.
The migration was successful and demonstrated scalability for a major e-commerce platform.
This suggests a potential industry trend toward using relational databases for high-concurrency state management previously dominated by in-memory stores like Redis.
